title: Deeply divided Israel braces for pivotal election
content_c:
Deeply divided Israel braces for pivotal election
- Published
After three years of regional war, this is a battle Israel always knew was coming.
The general election on Tuesday hangs over a country that's deeply divided and ready for a fight.
Polls published on Friday put the governing coalition and the main opposition bloc almost neck-and-neck, with half a million first-time voters due to cast their ballot and some 70,000 Israelis reportedly flying in from abroad specifically to vote.
On Saturday night, vast crowds of opposition voters gathered in central Tel Aviv to demand a change of government.
"We're optimistic," 21-year-old Omri told me. "I want peace, I want security, and I want to end corruption and get the religious fanatics out."
This campaign has been energized by new tactics - including AI videos designed to grab the headlines - and also by a new face.
Gadi Eisenkot is, perhaps, not the man you might expect to take on the flashy, aggressive, media-savvy brand of Israel's longest-serving prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu.
- How do Israel's elections work and who are the main contenders? 
  - Published12 hours ago
- Israel's far right find fertile ground among first-time voters 
  - Published5 days ago
- The bitter row over military service that could shape Israel's future 
  - Published1 day ago
Relatively new to politics, with a working-class Moroccan background, Eisenkot is a former military chief of staff who is renowned for his calm manner and low-drama approach. He's been dubbed by some as a "non-politician".
But he and his centrist Yashar party have regularly pipped Netanyahu and his Likud party to the top spot in recent polls, the last of which was published on Friday, in line with Israeli election law.
Israeli politics is the art of coalition-building, rather than the task of any one party winning power, but with the predicted result too close to call, Eisenkot's rising profile has sharpened a race many Israelis already see as existential for the future of their country.
I watched him slip past the cameras at a community centre for Ethiopian Jews in the city of Ramle last week, through a gaggle of security personnel and advisors.
One of those who had come to hear him speak was David, a smartly dressed man in a freshly-pressed shirt and navy jacket, who said he had met Eisenkot before.
"He looks you in the eye, not like a leader looking down at someone," David told me. "And he listens. He's very sympathetic."
Eisenkot's appeal is often put down to his personal manner and profile. A softly-spoken military man whose son was killed during the Gaza War, he has presented himself as coming "from the periphery", not from Israel's wealthy urban elite.
His Moroccan background became election headlines earlier this month when a pro-Netanyahu speaker used a racist slur to refer to Eisenkot during a TV debate, referring to him as a Moroccan "monkey".
"These elections are about many issues," Eisenkot told the crowd gathered at the Ramle community centre. "They are about security, economy, education...but primarily, they are about the identity of the State of Israel, and what kind of Israel we want to see. A Jewish state, a democratic state, a liberal, tolerant, egalitarian state."
This is music to opposition ears, who say Benjamin Netanyahu's government is a threat to Israel's democracy, pointing to his efforts to curb the powers of the judicial system, and his refusal to establish a state commission of inquiry into the 7 October 2023 attacks on the grounds that the country's Supreme Court would be biased against him.
Eisenkot, along with other opposition leaders, has attempted to draw voters away from Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party by promising such a state inquiry, which a recent survey suggests is supported by more than 70% of Jewish Israelis.
He has also vowed to enforce court rulings on drafting ultra-Orthodox Jews into national military service - another measure that is popular with right-wing voters and opposition alike.
Benjamin Netanyahu has hit back with a campaign focused on Israel's security, and a core campaign slogan of "No Surrender".
He has repeatedly cast his rivals as soft on security, playing on the fears of some right-wing voters that Jewish opposition parties might ally with Israel's Arab parties to secure a majority, and suggesting this could compromise national security.
Around one-fifth of Israel's population is Arab - many of whom describe themselves as Palestinian citizens of Israel.
These are the first elections since the 7 October attacks, in which Hamas-led gunmen stormed through Gaza's border fence, killing almost 1,200 people and taking 251 hostage.
It was Israel's worst security failure, but three years on its prime minister is again running for re-election as the only man who can keep Israel safe.
"If the army had woken him in time, it wouldn't have happened," Shlomi Bashar told me, one of several die-hard Netanyahu fans drinking in a basement café in Jerusalem's Mahane Yehuda market. "He does bear a certain responsibility, but after the 7 October, he changed the entire Middle East."
Netanyahu has been hammering home the message that Israel's wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran, in the years after the 7 October attacks, have reduced existential threats to the country.
"We need him to be re-elected so that he can finish this work," said Shlomi. "In my opinion, he is one of the best leaders in the world. Most of the world loves him and respects him, because he is a strong man and his ideas are correct."
The prime minister has traditionally relied on a stable base of right-wing voters, but is projected to see a thinning of support in this election. Some voters may be slipping away to opposition parties like Eisenkot's. Others, including some die-hard Likud voters we spoke to, said the 7 October attacks had pushed them towards parties further on the right.
Lt Col (Res) Eyal Hajbi, head of the regional civil defence unit in the Netanyahu stronghold of Sderot, right on the Gaza border, lost several friends and colleagues in the attacks. He lights candles for them every day in his office, and told me he would be thinking about them when he cast his ballot on Tuesday.
Standing on a ridge overlooking the ruins of northern Gaza, he gestured to the wasteland where Israel's army has completely flattened the neighbourhoods of Beit Lahia and Beit Hanoun.
"As far as I'm concerned, after 7 October, we should wipe them all out," he said. "I've changed my understanding of Gaza. Before, I wouldn't have said we should destroy it."
He told me he and his family had always voted Likud, but that now he was voting for the far-right party of Itamar Ben Gvir, Jewish Power.
"My family has become more extreme than it ever was before," he said. "If once we deliberated over it, today we don't think twice; we vote."
Polls suggest that less than 10% of Israelis are undecided and that very few of those are considering switching between government parties and opposition ones.
Ben Gvir, National Security minister in Netanyahu's coalition, has been reaching out to younger voters through headline-grabbing social media campaigns.
A poll for one of Israel's leading newspapers, Yedioth Ahronoth, published on 9 October, suggested that more than 16% of first-time voters in Israel would choose far-right parties like his.
In Sderot, a group of 18 year olds from a nearby Jewish religious college told me their political views had been affected by the 7 October attacks far more than their parents. All four teenagers were planning to vote for another far-right party, Religious Zionism, led by Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich.
"Today, the whole younger generation understands that peaceful paths will not work," Aviad Elmahach, one of the teenagers, told me. "Older adults, who are set in a fixed mindset, find [it] harder to change, but the youth understand that we need to be here with strength and an iron fist, which is the only way to win."
The lesson of 7 October, he said, was that Israel needed to be as forceful as possible in its relations with the Palestinians, more than 74,000 of whom have been killed by Israel in Gaza since then, according to the Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.
"The youth have a fresh new perspective that has not yet become entrenched in politics, and they understand very well why we're voting for Smotrich - it means holding the land with strength and giving [the Palestinians] nothing through peaceful gestures."
A little further south along the Gaza border are the kibbutzim that were overrun by gunmen during the Hamas attacks. They were renowned for decades as bastions of the Israeli left.
Among them is Nir Oz, where 47 people were killed and 76 taken hostage that day.
Three years on, residents are moving back. Twenty-six-year-old Gal Pauker has opened a Friday wine café at the edge of his small vineyard next to the Gaza border - a few wooden tables set out under sheets of beige canvas to shade customers from the strong desert sun. His grandfather Gideon was killed during the 7 October attacks.
I asked Gal, and his mother Galia, whether the those attacks had shifted their political views.
"We need a change - we can't live with this government anymore," Galia said. "And I'm not talking about security, I'm talking first about humanity."
Having voted for centrist parties in the past, Galia says she's decided to vote for Eisenkot this time around, because "he's an ordinary guy and I hope he'll continue the way he's talking".
Her son Gal said he was deciding between Eisenkot and the left-leaning Democrats party of Yair Golan, another former army general.
"I'm not naïve. I know there are a lot of more militant voices from young generations," he said. "I don't know if Eisenkot will be better than Golan in terms of security, but I think we have bigger problems: economics, social problems, education, health. We didn't get new neighbours on October 7 - it was a major event, but didn't change how we see ourselves."
Threats to security versus threats to democracy - these are old political tramlines for Israeli voters, deepened by the 7 October attacks, and by four years of the most right-wing government in Israel's history.
But on some of the biggest international concerns, the differences between government and opposition are not as wide as it might seem.
Gadi Eisenkot has pledged to end Hamas rule of Gaza within 18 months, either through a US-led peace plan, or through "military and operational capabilities".
All the main opposition leaders have voiced support for some form of Israeli settlement in the occupied West Bank, which has expanded massively under the current government and is illegal under international law. None have openly committed to the idea of full Palestinian statehood, something Benjamin Netanyahu has vowed to block. Eisenkot has spoken about creating the conditions for "autonomy or state-minus" under ultimate Israeli security control.
Tuesday's vote could well end in deadlock, with neither government nor opposition able to form a majority without the support of Arab parties, which polls project could win enough seats to be kingmakers. All but one of Israel's Jewish opposition parties have so far rejected working with either of the two Arab party blocs.
With Benjamin Netanyahu ramping up warnings of fresh threats from Iran, opposition voices warning of potential disruption to the ballot, and Israeli rights activists warning of a further spike in violence by settlers in the occupied West Bank, political instability at home could leave Israelis facing both a fresh test of their democracy, and fresh security threats.

"If the army had woken him in time, it wouldn't have happened," Shlomi Bashar told me, one of several die-hard Netanyahu fans drinking in a basement café in Jerusalem's Mahane Yehuda market. "He does bear a certain responsibility, but after the 7 October, he changed the entire Middle East."
Netanyahu has been hammering home the message that Israel's wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran, in the years after the 7 October attacks, have reduced existential threats to the country.
"We need him to be re-elected so that he can finish this work," said Shlomi. "In my opinion, he is one of the best leaders in the world. Most of the world loves him and respects him, because he is a strong man and his ideas are correct."
The prime minister has traditionally relied on a stable base of right-wing voters, but is projected to see a thinning of support in this election. Some voters may be slipping away to opposition parties like Eisenkot's. Others, including some die-hard Likud voters we spoke to, said the 7 October attacks had pushed them towards parties further on the right.
Lt Col (Res) Eyal Hajbi, head of the regional civil defence unit in the Netanyahu stronghold of Sderot, right on the Gaza border, lost several friends and colleagues in the attacks. He lights candles for them every day in his office, and told me he would be thinking about them when he cast his ballot on Tuesday.
Standing on a ridge overlooking the ruins of northern Gaza, he gestured to the wasteland where Israel's army has completely flattened the neighbourhoods of Beit Lahia and Beit Hanoun.
"As far as I'm concerned, after 7 October, we should wipe them all out," he said. "I've changed my understanding of Gaza. Before, I wouldn't have said we should destroy it."
He told me he and his family had always voted Likud, but that now he was voting for the far-right party of Itamar Ben Gvir, Jewish Power.
"My family has become more extreme than it ever was before," he said. "If once we deliberated over it, today we don't think twice; we vote."
Polls suggest that less than 10% of Israelis are undecided and that very few of those are considering switching between government parties and opposition ones.
Ben Gvir, National Security minister in Netanyahu's coalition, has been reaching out to younger voters through headline-grabbing social media campaigns.
A poll for one of Israel's leading newspapers, Yedioth Ahronoth, published on 9 October, suggested that more than 16% of first-time voters in Israel would choose far-right parties like his.
In Sderot, a group of 18 year olds from a nearby Jewish religious college told me their political views had been affected by the 7 October attacks far more than their parents. All four teenagers were planning to vote for another far-right party, Religious Zionism, led by Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich.
"Today, the whole younger generation understands that peaceful paths will not work," Aviad Elmahach, one of the teenagers, told me. "Older adults, who are set in a fixed mindset, find [it] harder to change, but the youth understand that we need to be here with strength and an iron fist, which is the only way to win."
The lesson of 7 October, he said, was that Israel needed to be as forceful as possible in its relations with the Palestinians, more than 74,000 of whom have been killed by Israel in Gaza since then, according to the Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.
"The youth have a fresh new perspective that has not yet become entrenched in politics, and they understand very well why we're voting for Smotrich - it means holding the land with strength and giving [the Palestinians] nothing through peaceful gestures."
A little further south along the Gaza border are the kibbutzim that were overrun by gunmen during the Hamas attacks. They were renowned for decades as bastions of the Israeli left.
Among them is Nir Oz, where 47 people were killed and 76 taken hostage that day.
Three years on, residents are moving back. Twenty-six-year-old Gal Pauker has opened a Friday wine café at the edge of his small vineyard next to the Gaza border - a few wooden tables set out under sheets of beige canvas to shade customers from the strong desert sun. His grandfather Gideon was killed during the 7 October attacks.
I asked Gal, and his mother Galia, whether the those attacks had shifted their political views.
"We need a change - we can't live with this government anymore," Galia said. "And I'm not talking about security, I'm talking first about humanity."
Having voted for centrist parties in the past, Galia says she's decided to vote for Eisenkot this time around, because "he's an ordinary guy and I hope he'll continue the way he's talking".
Her son Gal said he was deciding between Eisenkot and the left-leaning Democrats party of Yair Golan, another former army general.
"I'm not naïve. I know there are a lot of more militant voices from young generations," he said. "I don't know if Eisenkot will be better than Golan in terms of security, but I think we have bigger problems: economics, social problems, education, health. We didn't get new neighbours on October 7 - it was a major event, but didn't change how we see ourselves."
Threats to security versus threats to democracy - these are old political tramlines for Israeli voters, deepened by the 7 October attacks, and by four years of the most right-wing government in Israel's history.
But on some of the biggest international concerns, the differences between government and opposition are not as wide as it might seem.
Gadi Eisenkot has pledged to end Hamas rule of Gaza within 18 months, either through a US-led peace plan, or through "military and operational capabilities".
All the main opposition leaders have voiced support for some form of Israeli settlement in the occupied West Bank, which has expanded massively under the current government and is illegal under international law. None have openly committed to the idea of full Palestinian statehood, something Benjamin Netanyahu has vowed to block. Eisenkot has spoken about creating the conditions for "autonomy or state-minus" under ultimate Israeli security control.
Tuesday's vote could well end in deadlock, with neither government nor opposition able to form a majority without the support of Arab parties, which polls project could win enough seats to be kingmakers. All but one of Israel's Jewish opposition parties have so far rejected working with either of the two Arab party blocs.
With Benjamin Netanyahu ramping up warnings of fresh threats from Iran, opposition voices warning of potential disruption to the ballot, and Israeli rights activists warning of a further spike in violence by settlers in the occupied West Bank, political instability at home could leave Israelis facing both a fresh test of their democracy, and fresh security threats.

title: Board of Deputies of British Jews declares Greens to be racist party
content_c:
Board of Deputies of British Jews declares Greens to be racist party
- Published
The Green Party of England and Wales has been declared a racist organisation by the Board of Deputies of British Jews.
The Jewish body, which is the largest in the UK, was responding to the "Zionism is racism" policy motion passed at the Green Party's conference earlier this month.
Board of Deputies president Phil Rosenberg said a vote passed by 118 votes to one to declare that the Greens had, "by adopting an antisemitic platform, become a racist party".
A spokesman for the Greens insisted the party does not discriminate against people who hold Zionist views and said it rejected the Board of Deputies' "characterisation of this motion and our party".
They added the decision "will not stop us from speaking out against the genocide in Gaza and pushing for stronger sanctions against the Israeli government and its leaders". Israel has repeatedly denied its actions in Gaza amount to genocide.
The motion passed by the Board of Deputies urged other parties not to do deals with the Greens unless they rejected the policy.
Forming coalition deals with Greens at local or national level would be "failing to take antisemitism with the requisite seriousness", it said, unless the party's local leadership have rejected the policy and committed to overturn it.
Labour has already issued an ultimatum to local Green groups it is currently in coalition with, telling them to disown the motion or lose the party's support.
Rosenberg said: "By adopting an antisemitic platform, the Green Party of England and Wales has become a racist party. We will treat it accordingly.
"No political party has the right to tell Jews that a central part of our identity, rooted in thousands of years of history, faith and peoplehood, is racist.
"The Green Party's policy brands much of our community, including our synagogues and communal organisations, with that slur. It gives prejudice against Jews a political licence.
"The Green Party's leadership must now take responsibility for reversing this policy and confronting the antisemitism it has legitimised."
The motion backed by Green members at its party conference earlier this month said Zionism was an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state in historic Palestine to the exclusion and/ or domination of the non-Jewish population".
It was criticised by Jewish groups, as well as four Green MPs and two former leaders, and opposition political parties.
Responding when the Green motion was passed, the Board of Deputies and Jewish Leadership Council said in a joint statement that "Zionism is anti-racism, creating a refuge for Jews in their ancient homeland after millennia of persecution outside it".
Green Party leader Zack Polanski, who is Jewish, did not take part in the vote on the motion as he left the conference early to campaign in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election which was held days later.
He has since told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that, while he would like to make amendments, he would not overturn the motion, which would be party policy until 2028.

- Polanski faces greatest crisis of his leadership so far

title: Heating oil costs 'more than double' ahead of winter
content_c:
Heating oil costs 'more than double' ahead of winter
- Published
Households in Upper Teesdale are preparing for winter with the cost of heating oil "more than double" what it was compared to this time last year.
With no mains gas supply in Middleton-in-Teesdale, most homes in the area rely on heating oil to keep warm, meaning residents can face bills of more than £1,000 at a time to fill their tanks.
Recent figures suggest households across rural areas including Teesdale, Weardale, Northumberland and parts of North Yorkshire are currently paying around £600 for a 500-litre delivery of heating oil, equivalent to about £1.19 per litre.
In October 2025, domestic heating oil prices were around 52p per litre.
The rise is creating concern in communities where many residents have little choice but to rely on oil-fired heating systems.
Upper Teesdale Agricultural Support Services (UTASS), based in Middleton-in-Teesdale, run a heating oil buying group aimed at helping residents secure lower prices.
By combining orders from households across the area and placing monthly bulk purchases, the scheme can reduce costs by around 3p per litre.
The organisation says the group has become an important way of helping people manage household budgets during periods of high energy costs.
Emma Spry, the manager at UTASS, says the scheme helps with residents' "cash flow".
"To get a discount on oil you need to be buying more than 1000 litres at a time, with our scheme the minimum order is 500 litres so this can help to spread the cost a bit for people," Spry said.
UTASS itself relies on heating oil to warm its offices.
Kim Richardson, who has lived in Middleton in Teesdale for more than 20 years, said "the price of oil has shot up, it's double what it was last year".
"I need 1,000 litres, it'll be a fortune.
"My husband turns the heating off but I like it on, I like to be warm.
"Thankfully, the good summer we had meant we didn't need to use much oil during the summer months."
Many households in the area try to plan ahead by filling tanks during the warmer months when prices can sometimes be lower.
For some, however, the cost of heating oil is entirely unaffordable.
Pauline Thompson, who lives locally, says she does not use heating oil due to the cost, instead she uses oil filled radiators that use electricity to heat up.
"If we need hot water for a bath, I boil the kettle. Heating oil is just too expensive to use.
"When I moved in, I rang the electricity board and asked for the cheapest way to heat the house and they said oil radiators which use electricity to heat up so I use them instead, I'm on pension credits, it's just not affordable for me."
Without access to mains gas, residents have fewer options when heating costs increase.
As winter draws closer, organisations such as UTASS are encouraging anyone concerned about heating oil costs to explore schemes that could help reduce the price they pay.

title: Exiled opposition leader María Corina Machado returns to rapturous reception in Venezuela
content_c:
The Venezuelan opposition leader, María Corina Machado, has announced she has returned to Venezuela almost a year after she left the country to receive the Nobel peace prize.
“I’m here. With you,” she wrote on X on Sunday lunchtime.
Her close ally Edmundo González, who is in exile, confirmed her arrival. “Venezuela! I am thrilled to announce to you that our leader, my dear María Corina, is on Venezuelan soil,” he posted on social media.
“Today is a very important day for Venezuelans. Our sovereign voice returns with her to lead and guide this process!” he said, adding that he too would soon return.
It was not immediately clear how Machado, 59, had managed to return to Venezuela but footage on social media showed she was in Barquisimeto, the capital of Lara state, which is about 220 miles west of the capital, Caracas.
Images showed her surrounded by supporters holding mobile phones in the Sanctuary of the Divine Shepherdess church.
Footage posted on social media by her close ally Pedro Urruchurtu showed hundreds of supporters gathered outside the church to greet her, shouting: “Freedom! Freedom! Freedom!”
After leaving the church, it took Machado – festooned in rosaries handed to her by followers – eight hours to reach Caracas because of massive crowds lining and blocking streets and highways.
Tens of thousands of cheering supporters greeted Machado as she made her way to the capital on Sunday night. “This country is giving lessons to everyone,” she shouted as her convoy entered Caracas, leaning out of the sunroof to shake hands and hug raucous supporters.
“For the reunion of every family, for freedom of every political prisoner, for the freedom of Venezuela,” she wrote on social media.
The Trump administration had reportedly opposed Machado’s return, believing her presence would complicate the cosy relationship it has struck up with the interim president, Delcy Rodríguez, since abducting her former boss, Nicolás Maduro, in January.
Machado and Rodríguez are political arch-rivals.
Machado slipped out of Venezuela last December – a few weeks before Maduro’s capture – and in recent months has reportedly made more than half a dozen failed attempts to return home, including after the devastating earthquake that hit the northern coast in June.
After Maduro was seized, many had expected Donald Trump to give Machado his blessing to take power. Her movement is widely believed to have beaten Maduro in the 2024 presidential election, but he refused to hand over power.
Instead the US president embraced Rodríguez, Maduro’s vice-president, who now governs a country widely seen as a US protectorate.
Machado has repeatedly heaped praise on Trump for launching the operation to remove Maduro, and gave him her 2025 Nobel peace prize medal, which she had been awarded for her peaceful challenge to Venezuela’s authoritarian government.
Asked by reporters on Sunday about her return, Trump said: “I don’t know anything about it, but I think she’s a very nice woman. She gave me her Nobel prize, so how can I say anything else?
“I hope she’s safe. She’s a very nice woman. But we’re doing very well in Venezuela.”
The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, claimed credit for creating the conditions that allowed Machado’s safe return after 10 months in exile.
Her return “is the direct result of the US-supported reconciliation talks which has already seen hundreds of political prisoners freed and hundreds of political opposition figures return from exile”, he said.
From Barquisimeto, Machado headed east through the state of Yaracuy towards Caracas in a convoy of vehicles. Images released by aides show her reaching out from a car’s sunroof towards dozens of supporters who had gathered at the roadside to see her.
Members of Venezuela’s government have long hinted that Machado would be arrested if she tried to return as a result of her years-long struggle for political change. But there was no sign of the security services bothering her on Sunday as she moved towards the capital, perhaps suggesting Washington had sanctioned her return and instructed Rodríguez’s government not to react.
Machado has called for fresh presidential elections to be held by July 2027, but it is unclear whether the Trump administration supports that timeline given the lucrative partnership it has struck up with Rodríguez.
Trump announced what he called “the biggest oil deal in world history” with Venezuela in August, subsequently describing the agreement as the spoils of January’s brief “war”.

title: Demand for UK government action 10 months after British man’s death in Grenada
content_c:
A time-critical investigation into the death of a British father whose body was found in a ransacked property on the Caribbean island of Grenada has stalled because of diplomatic delays between the two countries.
Charity workers supporting the family of Andrew Frederick are demanding immediate government intervention to clear the path for a full investigation to begin almost 10 months after his death, which has been ruled a homicide by a pathologist.
The Murdered Abroad charity has called on the foreign affairs select committee to step in after Grenadian police found there was “no basis … that any homicide has occurred” and closed the case.
This was despite a report from an autopsy, done in the week he died, saying Frederick, 47, had suffered “blunt force trauma”, was tortured, including by removal of his toenail, and ruling the death a homicide.
Frederick’s body was found on 4 January. Since then, the family say they have been forced to focus on their fight for justice instead of coming to terms with their loss.
Murdered Abroad’s founder, Eve Henderson, said: “We understand there are challenges but [almost 10 months] on, this family is still being met with obfuscation. If a family this determined cannot get the FCDO [Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office] to put their diplomatic powers to good use, what hope is there for the 60 to 80 families bereaved by murder abroad each year?
“A minister must look urgently at how consular services treat these traumatised families or the foreign affairs select committee must step in,” she added.
A former Scotland Yard homicide commander who is supporting the family described Grenada’s actions as “incredible”.
“In the autopsy report … the pathologist, who is a qualified medical examiner, categorically states that he believes this is a case of homicide and that Andrew was tortured before he was killed,” David Johnston said. “And yet the police just choose to ignore that because it didn’t fit with their model. I mean, it’s incredible.”
After a sustained campaign by the family, British authorities became involved and Frederick’s body was repatriated to the UK in August, where a second autopsy was carried out, during which it was discovered his organs were missing.
The family described this discovery as “shocking and devastating”.
In a statement, they said: “We were already heartbroken that Andrew’s life was cruelly taken, but nothing could have prepared us for what we would learn afterwards. For six weeks after his death, Andrew’s body was held under the control of the Grenadian authorities. When he was later examined in the UK, parts of his neck and all of his organs, including his brain, heart, and lungs, were missing.
“That discovery has been shocking and absolutely devastating for our family; we are still struggling to process it. It has added pain upon pain and left us with deep hurt with so many unanswered questions. Despite our multiple inquiries, no one has told us where they are, what happened to them, or why we were never told. No family should ever have to ask these questions.”
Last month a UK coroner asked the Metropolitan police to conduct an investigation. Weeks later a communication from UK authorities, seen by the Guardian, said a British high commissioner had raised Frederick’s case with officials at the highest levels of government in Grenada, and indicated that authorities there had agreed to cooperate with any forthcoming formal request for the UK to assist with the investigation.
That formal request was sent weeks ago but the family say they are still waiting for Grenada “to honour their verbal commitment to the British high commissioner and approve the request to cooperate”.
“Every day for almost 10 months we have had to live without Andrew and without answers. A formal request from the UK, asking Grenada to cooperate with its investigation into Andrew’s death, still sits unsigned. It is the best chance we have of finding the truth,” the family statement said.
Johnston said the initial handling of Frederick’s case and the further delays could have a detrimental effect on the investigation.
“In a homicide investigation we have a phrase that we refer to as the golden hours, which are the first real 24 hours from the notification, or the discovery, of a homicide [which] are the most important and crucial … because evidence diminishes and can be lost if a crime scene is not properly noted and properly managed.
“In the case of the death of [Frederick] that’s exactly what happened … the police, in my view, failed to properly identify and preserve the crime scene and to treat the crime scene in the manner it should have been treated,” he said.
Johnston added that cooperation between British and Grenadian police could help to “bring some stability to that investigation”.
An FCDO spokesperson said: “We are supporting the family of a British man who died in Grenada, and are in contact with the local authorities.”
The Guardian has approached the Royal Grenada Police Force for comment but has not had a reply.

Continue reading...
author: Natricia Duncan
content:
A time-critical investigation into the death of a British father whose body was found in a ransacked property on the Caribbean island of Grenada has stalled because of diplomatic delays between the two countries.
Charity workers supporting the family of Andrew Frederick are demanding immediate government intervention to clear the path for a full investigation to begin almost 10 months after his death, which has been ruled a homicide by a pathologist.
The Murdered Abroad charity has called on the foreign affairs select committee to step in after Grenadian police found there was “no basis … that any homicide has occurred” and closed the case.
This was despite a report from an autopsy, done in the week he died, saying Frederick, 47, had suffered “blunt force trauma”, was tortured, including by removal of his toenail, and ruling the death a homicide.
Frederick’s body was found on 4 January. Since then, the family say they have been forced to focus on their fight for justice instead of coming to terms with their loss.
Murdered Abroad’s founder, Eve Henderson, said: “We understand there are challenges but [almost 10 months] on, this family is still being met with obfuscation. If a family this determined cannot get the FCDO [Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office] to put their diplomatic powers to good use, what hope is there for the 60 to 80 families bereaved by murder abroad each year?
“A minister must look urgently at how consular services treat these traumatised families or the foreign affairs select committee must step in,” she added.
A former Scotland Yard homicide commander who is supporting the family described Grenada’s actions as “incredible”.
“In the autopsy report … the pathologist, who is a qualified medical examiner, categorically states that he believes this is a case of homicide and that Andrew was tortured before he was killed,” David Johnston said. “And yet the police just choose to ignore that because it didn’t fit with their model. I mean, it’s incredible.”
After a sustained campaign by the family, British authorities became involved and Frederick’s body was repatriated to the UK in August, where a second autopsy was carried out, during which it was discovered his organs were missing.
The family described this discovery as “shocking and devastating”.
In a statement, they said: “We were already heartbroken that Andrew’s life was cruelly taken, but nothing could have prepared us for what we would learn afterwards. For six weeks after his death, Andrew’s body was held under the control of the Grenadian authorities. When he was later examined in the UK, parts of his neck and all of his organs, including his brain, heart, and lungs, were missing.
“That discovery has been shocking and absolutely devastating for our family; we are still struggling to process it. It has added pain upon pain and left us with deep hurt with so many unanswered questions. Despite our multiple inquiries, no one has told us where they are, what happened to them, or why we were never told. No family should ever have to ask these questions.”
Last month a UK coroner asked the Metropolitan police to conduct an investigation. Weeks later a communication from UK authorities, seen by the Guardian, said a British high commissioner had raised Frederick’s case with officials at the highest levels of government in Grenada, and indicated that authorities there had agreed to cooperate with any forthcoming formal request for the UK to assist with the investigation.
That formal request was sent weeks ago but the family say they are still waiting for Grenada “to honour their verbal commitment to the British high commissioner and approve the request to cooperate”.
“Every day for almost 10 months we have had to live without Andrew and without answers. A formal request from the UK, asking Grenada to cooperate with its investigation into Andrew’s death, still sits unsigned. It is the best chance we have of finding the truth,” the family statement said.
Johnston said the initial handling of Frederick’s case and the further delays could have a detrimental effect on the investigation.
“In a homicide investigation we have a phrase that we refer to as the golden hours, which are the first real 24 hours from the notification, or the discovery, of a homicide [which] are the most important and crucial … because evidence diminishes and can be lost if a crime scene is not properly noted and properly managed.
“In the case of the death of [Frederick] that’s exactly what happened … the police, in my view, failed to properly identify and preserve the crime scene and to treat the crime scene in the manner it should have been treated,” he said.
Johnston added that cooperation between British and Grenadian police could help to “bring some stability to that investigation”.
An FCDO spokesperson said: “We are supporting the family of a British man who died in Grenada, and are in contact with the local authorities.”
The Guardian has approached the Royal Grenada Police Force for comment but has not had a reply.
The family said: “With each passing day, our family’s heartbreak deepens. We need closure, and Grenada’s prime minister, who is also the minister of national security, can help make this possible. We appeal to him, with humanity and compassion, to sign the request without further delay.”
Additional reporting by Calistra Farrier

title: Protein shakes for teenagers: Good or bad idea?
content_c:
Protein shakes for teenagers: Good or bad idea?
October 25, 2026
You can take it as a powdered drink, or in a snack bar. Puddings and certain breads are also promoted as "sources of protein," and protein-enriched products like Kindershake and Teen Balance are specifically designed to appeal to a young people — and it appears to be working.
In a representative survey of almost 1,000 parents by the University of Michigan in 2024, just under half said their children, who were aged 13 to 17, had consumed protein products over the previous year. The survey found that boys were more likely to do so than girls, especially in connection with sport, or to build muscle. Girls took them to balance their diet, and to lose weight.
According to the statistics portal Statista, between March 2024 and March 2025 the fitness protein product market in Germany recorded a huge jump of around 25% in retail revenue.
How much protein do we actually need?
Proteins are key building blocks for our metabolism. They play an important role in building up and repairing tissue in our muscles, skin and organs. Proteins are the basis for the formation of enzymes that regulate chemical reactions in the body, and of antibodies that are vital for our immune system.
According to the German Nutrition Society (DGE), healthy adults should consume 0.8 grams of protein daily per kilogram of body weight. A woman weighing 65 kilos should eat 52 grams of protein per day, for example.
But they can do this without special protein products. A portion of oat flakes with an almond drink for breakfast, a baked potato with curd cheese for lunch, and two slices of wholemeal bread with peanut butter in the evening — objective achieved.
Young people should consume a little more, as they are still growing. For them, the formula is 0.9 grams of protein per kilo of body weight. A teenager weighing 45 kilos should therefore eat 40.5 grams of protein per day. People over 65 and children aged one to four should have a little more: one gram of protein per kilo of body weight.
Older people tend to eat too little protein, often because their appetite decreases. But a study done in Germany between 2015 and 2017 showed that children and young people there often consume too much. Around half of six- to 17-year-olds ate more than double the recommended daily amount of protein.
Can too much protein be dangerous?
Too much protein can be harmful in the long term, according to the DGE. Various studies show that children who eat too much protein, particularly animal protein, often become overweight. Some enter puberty early.
Above all, too much protein can put excessive strain on the kidneys, causing damage. The kidneys have to convert the amino acids that constitute the building blocks of proteins into urea before they are excreted in urine. Damage is particularly likely if a person doesn't drink enough fluids, or has pre-existing kidney damage — but adolescents are also at greater risk.
Protein helps build muscle and shed weight
A person's protein requirement is greater if they are very physically active. Among other things, according to a DGE position paper, proteins can help maintain or build up muscular mass and strength, and support recovery after strain.
The paper states that, depending on physical condition and what they are training for, sportspeople should consume between 1.2 and 2 grams of protein per kilo of body weight, divided into several portions throughout the day. These recommendations only apply to people who train for more than five hours a day.
Proteins are of interest to people who want to lose weight because they are good at satisfying hunger. People usually lose more weight by following a protein-rich diet rather than another. Long-term, though, the most important thing to look at is: How many calories am I consuming, and how many am I burning?
Is animal protein better than plant protein?
Overall, plant proteins usually contain somewhat fewer essential amino acids than animal protein. "Essential" because the body cannot make them by itself – it has to take them in as food.
However, wholegrain products, pulses, or nuts are also higher in fiber, vitamins, and unsaturated fats – all of which are healthy. The DGE therefore advises that protein intake should be increased primarily with sources of plant protein.
What is the criticism leveled against protein products?
Protein powders and bars are often enriched not only with vitamins and minerals but also with unhelpful ingredients like sweeteners, sugar, additives and flavorings. The German Sport University in Cologne even found doping substances in protein products that were praised for building muscle.
Adolescents in particular might experience an unpleasant side-effect of consuming protein powders. These usually consist of milk proteins. There are various ways in which milk proteins can increase the skin's production of sebum, and this can trigger or exacerbate acne, although a direct link between milk protein products and acne has not been definitively proven.
Specialists are also skeptical about protein shakes, fearing that they could lead to young people eating fewer normal meals, and thus consuming less fiber, micronutrients, and healthy fats.
'High protein content' = higher price
Protein-enriched foods are usually expensive. In a 2022 study, consumer organizations also found that foods that are naturally high in protein, such as cheese, curds, or soya drinks, often cost more if the protein content has been highlighted by the manufacturer.
Not even sportspeople with a high protein requirement need to supplement their diet with special protein products. The DGE advises that they should aim to satisfy their requirements by optimizing their diet, and says there is no scientific evidence that our bodies require protein-enriched food supplements when put under strain.
However, the experts do say that it may make sense for people to use protein preparations if they have allergies, problems with digestion, chewing, or swallowing, or if their appetite is very low.
This article has been translated from German.

title: Reisen in die Boom-Region: Merz und Steinmeier gleichzeitig in Asien
content_c:
Unabhängig voneinander Merz und Steinmeier reisen nach Asien
Kanzler Merz besucht ab heute Singapur, Japan und Südkorea - und dürfte versuchen, Partnerschaften auszubauen, um die Abhängigkeit von China zu reduzieren. Dort wiederum ist Bundespräsident Steinmeier zu Gast
"Außenkanzler" Friedrich Merz stört es nicht sonderlich, wenn er so bezeichnet wird - zumeist von Kritikern. Eher im Gegenteil. Ein deutscher Bundeskanzler müsse sich um die Außenpolitik kümmern, betont Merz immer wieder und schiebt nach: "Außenpolitik, Außenwirtschaftspolitik und Wirtschaftspolitik gehen Hand in Hand." Deshalb spreche er auf seinen Auslandsreisen immer auch über die strategischen wirtschaftlichen Interessen Deutschlands.
Das gilt für seine fünftägige Reise in den Indopazifikraum ganz besonders: Singapur, Japan und Südkorea - alle drei Länder seien "für uns zentral, um kritische, einseitige Abhängigkeiten abzubauen", sagte der Kanzler, als er die Asien-Reise Mitte Oktober in seiner Regierungserklärung im Bundestag ankündigte. "Das ist gegenwärtig eine Schlüsselaufgabe unserer interessengeleiteten Außenpolitik und unserer Wirtschaftspolitik", unterstrich der CDU-Chef.
Sorgen wegen unfairer Wettbewerbsbedingungen
Abhängigkeiten abbauen: Gemeint ist damit vor allem die Volksrepublik China. Der Gigant, der wirtschaftlich, technologisch, geopolitisch und militärisch alles in der Indopazifik-Region dominiert - mit Ambitionen weit darüber hinaus. Umso interessanter, dass Bundespräsident Frank-Walter Steinmeier parallel zur Reise des Kanzlers zum Staatsbesuch nach China fährt. Aus Regierungskreisen heißt es, der Besuch des Bundespräsidenten werde mutmaßlich stark dadurch geprägt sein, dass er zu einem Moment stattfinde, "zu dem Deutschland seine Chinapolitik neu austariert". Dazu sei in den vergangenen Wochen einiges entschieden worden.
In Deutschland und Europa gibt es große Sorgen wegen unfairer Wettbewerbsbedingungen im Handel mit dem Riesenreich. Hohe staatliche staatlichen Subventionen Pekings, Überkapazitäten in der Produktion und aggressive Preise schaden der deutschen Wirtschaft massiv - ebenso wie die von China künstlich niedrig gehaltene Landeswährung.
"Wir sehen nicht länger tatenlos zu", kündigte Friedrich Merz in seiner Regierungserklärung an, ohne die Volksrepublik namentlich zu nennen. "Wer mit uns den Handelskonflikt sucht, der wird spüren, dass wir uns jetzt zur Wehr setzen - und zwar mit angemessenen Reaktionen", betonte der Kanzler und verwies auf neue Handelsschutzinstrumente, die die EU-Kommission plant.
Treffen Steinmeiers mit Xi geplant
Aus dem Bundespräsidialamt heißt es, Steinmeier wolle bei seinem Besuch über die problematischen Wirtschaftsbeziehungen sprechen, über Fairness und wie sich Handelskonflikte vermeiden lassen. Ein Treffen mit Staats- und Parteichef Xi Jinping ist für Freitag geplant. Dann dürfte es auch um den Krieg in der Ukraine gehen. Der Bundespräsident wolle darum werben, dass China seinen Einfluss auf Russland nutzt, um die Angriffe zu beenden und ernsthafte Verhandlungen über ein Ende des Krieges zu ermöglichen.
Der Ukraine-Krieg wird auch am Rande der Kanzler-Reise eine Rolle spielen, wenn Merz politische Gespräche mit den jeweiligen Regierungschefs von Singapur, Japan und Südkorea führt. Bei den diversen Terminen des Kanzlers geht es aber vor allem darum, die Partnerschaft mit diesen drei wichtigen Industrieländern auszubauen. "De-risking", Steigerung der Wettbewerbsfähigkeit und Innovation - darum solle es unter anderem gehen, heißt es in Regierungskreisen.
Singapur als zentraler Wirtschafts-Knotenpunkt
"Wenn der Kanzler jetzt nach Singapur, Japan und Südkorea fährt, dann trifft er in das Herz unserer Ambitionen, mit diesen Industriepartnern mehr zu tun", sagt Wolfgang Niedermark, Mitglied der Hauptgeschäftsführung des Bundesverbandes der Deutschen Industrie (BDI). Japan ist nach China der zweitwichtigste Handelspartner Deutschlands in Asien, Südkorea liegt auf Platz drei. Der Insel- und Stadtstaat Singapur gilt als der zentrale Wirtschaftsknotenpunkt für Südostasien und den Indopazifik.
"Wir haben in den vergangenen Jahren vielleicht zu sehr auf den natürlich maßgeblichen Industriepartner China gesetzt", sagt der ausgewiesene Asien-Experte Niedermark. "Wir sehen jetzt aus verschiedensten Gründen, die hauptsächlich geopolitisch sind, aber auch im industriellen Wettbewerb mit China, dass wir das Risiko anders verteilen müssen."
"Asien-Pazifik-Konferenz der Deutschen Wirtschaft" in Seoul
Niedermark und andere BDI-Spitzenvertreter reisen in dieser Woche zunächst nach China und von dort weiter nach Seoul. In der südkoreanischen Hauptstadt findet vom 29. bis 31. Oktober die "Asien-Pazifik-Konferenz der Deutschen Wirtschaft" statt. Das hochrangige Treffen mit rund 1.000 Teilnehmern aus Politik, Wirtschaft und Wissenschaft wird am Donnerstag von Merz eröffnet.
Wirtschaftsministerin Katherina Reiche (CDU) übernimmt zusammen mit Siemens-Vorstandschef Roland Busch die Leitung der Konferenz. "Es ist gut und wichtig, diese Beziehungen zu pflegen", betont der BDI-Repräsentant Niedermark und verweist auf die hochrangige Wirtschaftsdelegation, die den Bundeskanzler in der Regierungsmaschine nach Asien begleitet. An Bord sind unter anderem Vertreter aus den Bereichen der Industrie- und Technologieunternehmen, der Verteidigung und der Energie. Die Namen von Teilnehmern gibt die Bundesregierung aber gewöhnlich bis zum Abflug nicht bekannt.
Niedermark findet es "klasse", dass Merz und Steinmeier gleichzeitig in die boomende Region Asien-Indopazifik reisen. Nötig sei ein Engagement auf verschiedenen Spuren: "Wir müssen mit China weiter im Gespräch bleiben. Wir müssen aber gleichzeitig neue Allianzen mit etablierten und neuen Partnern in der Region Asien suchen."

In Deutschland und Europa gibt es große Sorgen wegen unfairer Wettbewerbsbedingungen im Handel mit dem Riesenreich. Hohe staatliche staatlichen Subventionen Pekings, Überkapazitäten in der Produktion und aggressive Preise schaden der deutschen Wirtschaft massiv - ebenso wie die von China künstlich niedrig gehaltene Landeswährung.
"Wir sehen nicht länger tatenlos zu", kündigte Friedrich Merz in seiner Regierungserklärung an, ohne die Volksrepublik namentlich zu nennen. "Wer mit uns den Handelskonflikt sucht, der wird spüren, dass wir uns jetzt zur Wehr setzen - und zwar mit angemessenen Reaktionen", betonte der Kanzler und verwies auf neue Handelsschutzinstrumente, die die EU-Kommission plant.
Treffen Steinmeiers mit Xi geplant
Aus dem Bundespräsidialamt heißt es, Steinmeier wolle bei seinem Besuch über die problematischen Wirtschaftsbeziehungen sprechen, über Fairness und wie sich Handelskonflikte vermeiden lassen. Ein Treffen mit Staats- und Parteichef Xi Jinping ist für Freitag geplant. Dann dürfte es auch um den Krieg in der Ukraine gehen. Der Bundespräsident wolle darum werben, dass China seinen Einfluss auf Russland nutzt, um die Angriffe zu beenden und ernsthafte Verhandlungen über ein Ende des Krieges zu ermöglichen.
Der Ukraine-Krieg wird auch am Rande der Kanzler-Reise eine Rolle spielen, wenn Merz politische Gespräche mit den jeweiligen Regierungschefs von Singapur, Japan und Südkorea führt. Bei den diversen Terminen des Kanzlers geht es aber vor allem darum, die Partnerschaft mit diesen drei wichtigen Industrieländern auszubauen. "De-risking", Steigerung der Wettbewerbsfähigkeit und Innovation - darum solle es unter anderem gehen, heißt es in Regierungskreisen.
Singapur als zentraler Wirtschafts-Knotenpunkt
"Wenn der Kanzler jetzt nach Singapur, Japan und Südkorea fährt, dann trifft er in das Herz unserer Ambitionen, mit diesen Industriepartnern mehr zu tun", sagt Wolfgang Niedermark, Mitglied der Hauptgeschäftsführung des Bundesverbandes der Deutschen Industrie (BDI). Japan ist nach China der zweitwichtigste Handelspartner Deutschlands in Asien, Südkorea liegt auf Platz drei. Der Insel- und Stadtstaat Singapur gilt als der zentrale Wirtschaftsknotenpunkt für Südostasien und den Indopazifik.
"Wir haben in den vergangenen Jahren vielleicht zu sehr auf den natürlich maßgeblichen Industriepartner China gesetzt", sagt der ausgewiesene Asien-Experte Niedermark. "Wir sehen jetzt aus verschiedensten Gründen, die hauptsächlich geopolitisch sind, aber auch im industriellen Wettbewerb mit China, dass wir das Risiko anders verteilen müssen."
"Asien-Pazifik-Konferenz der Deutschen Wirtschaft" in Seoul
Niedermark und andere BDI-Spitzenvertreter reisen in dieser Woche zunächst nach China und von dort weiter nach Seoul. In der südkoreanischen Hauptstadt findet vom 29. bis 31. Oktober die "Asien-Pazifik-Konferenz der Deutschen Wirtschaft" statt. Das hochrangige Treffen mit rund 1.000 Teilnehmern aus Politik, Wirtschaft und Wissenschaft wird am Donnerstag von Merz eröffnet.
Wirtschaftsministerin Katherina Reiche (CDU) übernimmt zusammen mit Siemens-Vorstandschef Roland Busch die Leitung der Konferenz. "Es ist gut und wichtig, diese Beziehungen zu pflegen", betont der BDI-Repräsentant Niedermark und verweist auf die hochrangige Wirtschaftsdelegation, die den Bundeskanzler in der Regierungsmaschine nach Asien begleitet. An Bord sind unter anderem Vertreter aus den Bereichen der Industrie- und Technologieunternehmen, der Verteidigung und der Energie. Die Namen von Teilnehmern gibt die Bundesregierung aber gewöhnlich bis zum Abflug nicht bekannt.
Niedermark findet es "klasse", dass Merz und Steinmeier gleichzeitig in die boomende Region Asien-Indopazifik reisen. Nötig sei ein Engagement auf verschiedenen Spuren: "Wir müssen mit China weiter im Gespräch bleiben. Wir müssen aber gleichzeitig neue Allianzen mit etablierten und neuen Partnern in der Region Asien suchen."

title: Stichwahl in Brasilien: Kopf-an-Kopf-Rennen zwischen Lula und Bolsonaro
content_c:
Brasilien: Kopf-an-Kopf-Rennen zwischen Lula und Bolsonaro
25. Oktober 2026
Das zehntgrößte Industrieland Brasilien geht an diesem Sonntag erneut an die Wahlurnen. In der Stichwahl stehen sich der langjährige Präsident Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva von der Arbeiterpartei (PT) und der rechtspopulistische Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), Sohn des Ex-Präsidenten Jair Bolsonaro, gegenüber.
Umfragen deuten darauf hin, dass die Wahl äußerst knapp ausfallen dürfte. Beide Kandidaten liegen regelmäßig innerhalb der statistischen Fehlermarge gleichauf, was auf ein schwer vorhersehbares Ergebnis hindeutet.
In einer am Samstag veröffentlichten Umfrage des Meinungsforschungsinstituts Datafolha kam Flávio auf 51 Prozent der gültigen Stimmen, gegenüber 49 Prozent für Lula. Angesichts einer Fehlermarge von zwei Prozentpunkten gilt dieses Ergebnis jedoch als statistisches Unentschieden.
Eine am selben Tag veröffentlichte Nexus-Umfrage sah Flávio bei 50,5 Prozent und Lula bei 49,5 Prozent. Auch hier liegt der Abstand innerhalb der Fehlermarge von 2,2 Prozentpunkten.
Vorsprung aus dem ersten Wahlgang für Flávio
Im ersten Wahlgang am 4. Oktober hatte Flávio 47,03 Prozent der Stimmen erreicht, während Lula lediglich auf 45,16 Prozent kam. Der Abstand betrug damit lediglich 1,87 Prozentpunkte.
Neben den gleichen Nachnamen wie bei der letzten Wahl bringt die Stichwahl erneut eine entscheidende Auseinandersetzung zwischen zwei politischen Projekten mit sich, die gegensätzlicher kaum sein könnten.
Auf der einen Seite setzt Lula erneut auf die Erinnerung an sozialpolitische Maßnahmen, die während seiner früheren Regierungen (2003 bis 2011) eingeführt wurden, ergänzt durch Appelle zur Verteidigung der nationalen Souveränität.
Flávio hingegen setzt auf Revanche und will seine politische Dynastie nach der Niederlage von 2022 wieder an die Macht bringen. Ähnlich wie sein Vater verfolgt er eine Strategie, die auf die Ablehnung der PT in Teilen der brasilianischen Gesellschaft baut.
Zudem setzt er auf eine Konfrontationskurs gegenüber Institutionen wie dem Obersten Bundesgericht (STF) und greift Themen wie die steigenden Lebenshaltungskosten auf.
Rechtsruck in der Region?
Beide Wahlkämpfe standen zudem im Schatten der ethischen und institutionellen Krise der Justiz, des Aufflammens von Korruptionsskandalen, geopolitischer Spannungen und sogar von Vorwürfen ausländischer Einflussnahme, sowohl durch die US-Regierung als auch großer US-Technologiekonzerne.
Das Wahlergebnis wird auch die Rolle beeinflussen, die Brasilien in der Welt einnimmt. Ein möglicher Sieg von Lula im größten Land Südamerikas würde sowohl in Europa, dessen Staaten sich nach der Ära Jair Bolsonaro wieder Brasilien angenähert haben, als auch bei Verfechtern des Multilateralismus und von Umweltanliegen mit Erleichterung aufgenommen werden.
Ein Sieg Flávio Bolsonaros würde nicht nur bei Umweltschützern Besorgnis auslösen, sondern Brasilien voraussichtlich auch stärker an den USA unter Donald Trump ausrichten. Damit würde das Land einem Trend folgen, der bereits in anderen Staaten der Region zu beobachten ist, etwa in Argentinien unter Javier Milei und im Kolumbien von Abelardo de la Espriella.
Gestiegene Lebenshaltungskosten
Brasiliens Stichwahl findet nur wenige Tage vor dem siebten Jahrestag von Lulas Freilassung aus dem Hauptquartier der Bundespolizei in Curitiba statt. Der Präsident hatte dort 580 Tage in Haft verbracht.
Nach seiner Freilassung vollzog Lula nicht einmal drei Jahre später eine der spektakulärsten politischen Wendungen der brasilianischen Geschichte, als er 2022 den damaligen Präsidenten Jair Bolsonaro besiegte und eine dritte Amtszeit gewann.
Während seiner dritten Amtszeit seit 2023 zeigten zahlreiche wirtschaftliche Kennzahlen Brasiliens nach dem Rückgang am Ende der Amtszeit von Jair Bolsonaro Anzeichen einer Verbesserung.
Das Land erreichte Rekordwerte bei der Beschäftigung sowie die niedrigsten Armuts- und Extremarmutsraten seit Beginn der Datenerhebung im Jahr 2012. Diesen Verbesserungen standen allerdings stark gestiegenen Lebenshaltungskosten gegenüber.
Nach erstem Wahlgang
Da Lula sich inzwischen seinem 81. Geburtstag nähert, könnte dies die letzte Präsidentschaftswahl sein, bei der sein Name auf dem Stimmzettel steht. Im Wahlkampf 2026 setzte er erneut auf sein politisches Erbe und seine persönliche Lebensgeschichte.
Obwohl er in den Umfragen zunächst vorne lag, erwies sich der erste Wahlgang für den PT-Politiker als schwieriger als erwartet. Im Vergleich zur ersten Runde der Wahl von 2022 verlor Lula rund 3,4 Millionen Stimmen.
Lulas Wahlkampfteam reagierte nach der Enttäuschung über das Ergebnis der ersten Runde mit einer umfassenden Mobilisierung ihrer Anhängerschaft und einem verstärkten digitalen Auftritt, um den Rückstand noch aufzuholen.
Flávio Bolsonaro: Amnestie für seinen Vater?
Flávio hingegen geht, von einer Rechtswelle getragen, die im ersten Wahlgang den Nationalkongress erfasste, als Favorit in die Stichwahl.
Der 45-Jährige versprach, seinem Vater Jair Bolsonaro, der wegen eines versuchten Staatsstreichs verurteilt und inhaftiertwurde, "Gerechtigkeit widerfahren zu lassen". Er sprach sich mehrfach für eine Amnestie aller Beteiligten an den Angriffen am 8. Januar 2023 aus.
Daneben konzentrierte Flávio seinen Wahlkampf auf die Kritik an den steigenden Lebenshaltungskosten, die Themen Korruption und Drogen. Er versprach einen "Krieg" gegen das, was er als "Narkoterrorismus" bezeichnete, und orientierte sich damit an anderen Vertretern der lateinamerikanischen extremen Rechten, wie etwa dem salvadorianischen Präsidenten Nayib Bukele.
In der letzten Debatte vor den Wahlen beim TV-Sender Globo erklärte Flávio: "Lula hat Rindersteaks versprochen und Kürbis geliefert".
Lula: "Machen Sie dieses Experiment nicht"
Lula hingegen fasste zusammen, was aus seiner Sicht auf dem Spiel steht: "Entweder wir halten die Demokratie am Leben, oder wir werden einen Milizionär haben, der dieses Land regiert. Das ist für niemanden gut. Machen Sie dieses Experiment nicht", warnte er.
Da Umfragen zeigen, dass die Wählerschaft beider Kandidaten weitgehend festgelegt ist . So geben bei Flávio Bolsonaro beispielsweise 94 Prozent seiner Anhänger an, ihre Wahlentscheidung nicht mehr ändern zu wollen.
Lulas größte Herausforderung besteht in der Stichwahl daher darin, die kleine Gruppe der Unentschlossenen noch für sich zu gewinnen und jene Wähler zu mobilisieren, die im ersten Wahlgang nicht abgestimmt haben.
Sollte Flávio gewählt werden, würde er als Präsident über einen stärkeren politischen Rückhalt verfügen als einst sein Vater im Jahr 2018. Denn im brasilianischen Kongress könnte er mit der Unterstützung von einer Rekordzahl an neu gewählten Abgeordneten und Senatoren seiner Partei PL rechnen.
Dieser Artikel wurde aus dem Portugiesischen ins Deutsche adaptiert.
description: Feiert Bolsonaro ein Comeback? Flavio Bolsonaro, Sohn des Ex-Präsidenten, geht als Favorit in die Stichwahl gegen Amtsinhaber Lula. Umfragen sagen ein Kopf-an-Kopf Rennen voraus. Und eine Zerreißprobe für das Land.

title: День ангела 26 жовтня: кого та як вітати з іменинами
content_c:
День ангела 26 жовтня: кого та як вітати з іменинами
26 жовтня 2026 року — який нині день ангела та як вітати з іменинами — читайте в матеріалі ТСН.ua.
Хто святкує день ангела 26 жовтня
26 жовтня 2026 року привітайте з іменинами Антона, Василя, Дмитра, Опанаса.
Антон — латинське походження, означає «вступати в бій». В дитинстві вміє розташовувати до себе, любить бути в центрі уваги. В дорослому віці стає волелюбним, мужнім.
Василь — давньогрецьке ім’я, перекладається як «цар». В дитинстві оптиміст, життєлюб. В дорослому віці стає працелюбним, ініціативним.
Дмитро — давньогрецьке коріння, тлумачиться як «присвячений Деметрі». В дитинстві імпульсивний, активний. В дорослому віці стає рішучим, прямолінійним.
Опанас — давньогрецьке походження, означає «безсмертний». В дитинстві добрий, м’який. В дорослому віці стає комунікабельним, доброзичливим.
День ангела 26 жовтня — душевні привітання в прозі
Вітаю з Днем ангела! Нехай твій небесний охоронець завжди буде поруч, оберігає від негараздів, допомагає долати труднощі та веде до щастя. Бажаю міцного здоров’я, душевного спокою, щирої любові й багато радісних моментів у житті!
***
З Днем ангела! Нехай у твоєму серці завжди живуть віра, надія та любов, а кожен день приносить добрі новини, приємні зустрічі й нові можливості. Бажаю, щоб ангел-охоронець захищав тебе від усього лихого, а доля щедро дарувала щастя, добробут і благополуччя!
***
Щиро вітаю з іменинами! Бажаю, щоб твій ангел завжди розправляв над тобою свої крила, оберігав від біди та допомагав знаходити правильний шлях. Нехай у домі панують затишок і достаток, у душі — гармонія, а поруч будуть лише добрі, щирі та люблячі люди!
***
Зі святом твого небесного покровителя! Нехай кожен день буде наповнений світлом, теплом і приємними несподіванками. Бажаю здоров’я, яке не підводить, щастя, яке примножується, любові, яка зігріває, та мрій, які обов’язково здійснюються. Нехай ангел-охоронець завжди підтримує тебе й дарує впевненість у завтрашньому дні!
***
Вітаю з Днем ангела! Нехай твій небесний захисник оберігає кожен крок, відводить від тебе тривоги та наповнює життя Божим благословенням. Бажаю миру в душі, тепла в серці, достатку в оселі й безлічі приводів для усмішки. Нехай поруч завжди будуть люди, з якими легко, радісно та затишно!

Вітаю з Днем ангела! Нехай твій небесний охоронець завжди буде поруч, оберігає від негараздів, допомагає долати труднощі та веде до щастя. Бажаю міцного здоров’я, душевного спокою, щирої любові й багато радісних моментів у житті!
***
З Днем ангела! Нехай у твоєму серці завжди живуть віра, надія та любов, а кожен день приносить добрі новини, приємні зустрічі й нові можливості. Бажаю, щоб ангел-охоронець захищав тебе від усього лихого, а доля щедро дарувала щастя, добробут і благополуччя!
***
Щиро вітаю з іменинами! Бажаю, щоб твій ангел завжди розправляв над тобою свої крила, оберігав від біди та допомагав знаходити правильний шлях. Нехай у домі панують затишок і достаток, у душі — гармонія, а поруч будуть лише добрі, щирі та люблячі люди!
***
Зі святом твого небесного покровителя! Нехай кожен день буде наповнений світлом, теплом і приємними несподіванками. Бажаю здоров’я, яке не підводить, щастя, яке примножується, любові, яка зігріває, та мрій, які обов’язково здійснюються. Нехай ангел-охоронець завжди підтримує тебе й дарує впевненість у завтрашньому дні!
***
Вітаю з Днем ангела! Нехай твій небесний захисник оберігає кожен крок, відводить від тебе тривоги та наповнює життя Божим благословенням. Бажаю миру в душі, тепла в серці, достатку в оселі й безлічі приводів для усмішки. Нехай поруч завжди будуть люди, з якими легко, радісно та затишно!

title: День памяти преподобного Нестора Летописца: запреты и народные приметы
content_c:
27 октября украинцы отмечают День памяти преподобного Нестора Летописца. Раньше этот праздник отмечался 9 ноября, но в 2023 году дата празднования изменилась. С этим днём связаны определённые запреты.
Что нельзя делать в этот день
С давних времён украинцы соблюдали определённые запреты в этот день.
27 октября желательно не ссориться и не злословить. Не следует оскорблять других и желать кому-то зла.
В этот день также нельзя переедать — лучше ограничить себя в еде, молиться и собраться с мыслями.
Также в этот день нельзя давать обещания, которые вы не сможете выполнить. Считается, что если о них забыть или просто не выполнить, то вас могут ждать неприятности.
Творческие люди в этот день старались не принимать цветы. Существовало поверье, что слава может угаснуть, если принять подарок.
Раньше в этот праздник старались не много работать и не злоупотреблять алкоголем. В этот день не ходили в гости, чтобы не вынести счастье из своего дома.
Народные приметы 27 октября
Утром на деревьях виден иней — днём ждите мороза.
Если утром туман — ждите оттепели.
Гусь долго плавает на воде — холодов ещё не будет.
Если дует сильный ветер в одну сторону — в ближайший день пойдут осадки.
Если на сырую землю падает снег — весной рано зацветут подснежники.

title: Що їсти, щоб шкіра довше була молодою
content_c:
Що їсти, щоб шкіра довше була молодою
  - Author, Мелісса Гогенбум
  - Role, ВВС
- Published
- Час прочитання: 5 хв
Шкіра захищає нас протягом усього життя. Але з роками вона змінюється: втрачає пружність, стає сухішою, з'являються зморшки.
На це впливають не лише вік і сонце.
Забруднене повітря та інші чинники також можуть прискорювати старіння шкіри, пояснює Жан Крутманн, професор дерматології з університету Лейбніца.
Зупинити час неможливо, але можна допомогти шкірі довше залишатися здоровою. І важливу роль тут відіграє харчування.
Ось які продукти варто частіше додавати до свого раціону.
1. Яскраві фрукти та овочі
Морква, помідори, солодкий перець та інші різнокольорові овочі й фрукти багаті на антиоксиданти.
Вони допомагають захищати клітини шкіри від пошкоджень, спричинених сонцем і забрудненням повітря.
Особливо корисні каротиноїди - рослинні пігменти, які надають продуктам яскравого кольору.
"Ці речовини накопичуються в жировій тканині й допомагають захищати організм від ультрафіолетового випромінювання", - пояснює Фолькер Бьом, професор харчової хімії Єнського університету імені Фрідріха Шиллера.
Звісно, це не означає, що тепер можна відмовитися від сонцезахисного крему. Але є нюанс: багато хто користується ним лише перед тривалим перебуванням на сонці, а не щодня.
Продукти, багаті на каротиноїди, можуть стати додатковим джерелом захисту протягом року.
За словами Бьома, цей захист умовно можна порівняти з SPF 2-3. Однак він не замінює сонцезахисного засобу.
Є й маленький секрет: щоб організм краще засвоював каротиноїди, додавайте до моркви чи помідорів трохи жиру, наприклад оливкової олії.
Бета-каротин також перетворюється в організмі на вітамін А. Він потрібен для оновлення клітин шкіри та допомагає підтримувати її захисні функції.
Каротиноїди можуть сприяти й виробленню гіалуронової кислоти. Вона допомагає шкірі утримувати вологу, залишатися пружною та еластичною. Саме тому гіалуронову кислоту часто додають до зволожувальних кремів.
Ще одна можлива перевага - вплив на колаген та еластин, білки, які відповідають за пружність шкіри.
У невеликому дослідженні жінки протягом десяти місяців щодня приймали добавки з каротиноїдами. У результаті показники колагену й еластину в їхній шкірі покращилися. Це може свідчити про те, що каротиноїди допомагають підтримувати пружність шкіри.
А ще різнокольорові овочі та фрукти пов'язують зі здоровішим виглядом шкіри - тим самим природним сяйвом, яке часто асоціюється з молодістю.
Щоправда, миттєвого ефекту чекати не варто. Щоб антиоксиданти почали помітно впливати на захист шкіри, потрібен час.
"Зазвичай для цього потрібно від восьми до десяти тижнів", - пояснює професор Крутманн.
Корисним для шкіри є також манго.
В одному з досліджень під керівництвом Вів'єн Фам з Каліфорнійського університету взяли участь жінки в постменопаузі. Протягом 16 тижнів вони їли по 85 г манго чотири рази на тиждень.
В учасниць стали менш помітними вже наявні зморшки, а також зменшилася кількість нових.
На думку вчених, такий ефект може бути пов'язаний з високим вмістом каротиноїдів та інших антиоксидантів, зокрема флавоноїдів і мангіферину. Однак, щоб підтвердити ці висновки, потрібні додаткові дослідження.
Цікаво, що під час того самого експерименту виявили й протилежний ефект: у жінок, які щодня з'їдали близько 250 г манго, кількість зморшок збільшувалася.
Роберт Гекман, професор дієтології Каліфорнійського університету й один зі співавторів дослідження, визнає, що причина поки що незрозуміла. Можливо, річ у високому вмісті природних цукрів у манго.
"Ми припускаємо, що цукор спричиняв пошкодження молекул шкіри", - пояснює вчений.
Дослідження було невеликим, але, за словами Гекмана, подальша робота, результати якої ще не опубліковані, підтвердила початкові спостереження.
Манго та цитрусові також багаті на вітамін С. Він необхідний для вироблення колагену й водночас діє як антиоксидант, допомагаючи захищати шкіру від пошкоджень, спричинених сонцем.
Дослідження свідчать, що вітамін С може покращувати зволоженість шкіри та зменшувати пігментацію. Саме тому його широко використовують у косметичних засобах і харчових добавках, зазначає Крутманн.
2. Горіхи, насіння та жирна риба
Я ніколи особливо не любила мигдаль і волоські горіхи. Але нещодавно почала подрібнювати їх і додавати до салатів. І, на власний подив, виявила, що так вони мені подобаються набагато більше.
Виявилося, що це ще й корисна звичка для шкіри.
У невеликому рандомізованому дослідженні учасники, які протягом 16 тижнів перекушували мигдалем, мали менш помітні зморшки, ніж ті, хто обирав інші перекуси.
Горіхи та насіння також містять вітамін Е. Він захищає клітини від пошкоджень і допомагає підтримувати здоров'я шкіри. Якщо цього вітаміну бракує, шкіра може страждати, а рани - гоїтися повільніше.
Де шукати вітамін Е? У мигдалі, фундуку, кедрових горіхах і рослинних оліях.
Крім того, горіхи містять омега-6 жирні кислоти, які допомагають зміцнювати захисний бар'єр шкіри й утримувати в ній вологу.
Ще один важливий різновид корисних жирів - омега-3. Їх багато в жирній рибі, зокрема в лососі, сардинах і скумбрії. Вони також містяться в деяких водоростях.
Невеликі дослідження свідчать, що омега-3 можуть допомагати шкірі краще протистояти сонячному випромінюванню й захищати її від пошкоджень.
Жирна риба також може сприяти збереженню колагену та зменшенню запальних процесів в організмі.
3. Продукти, корисні для кишківника
Є ще один важливий момент: здоров'я шкіри залежить не лише від того, що ми їмо, а й від того, як працює наш кишківник.
Як це працює?
Коли ми їмо різноманітну рослинну їжу, корисні мікроорганізми в кишківнику виробляють речовини, які допомагають боротися із запаленням і захищають клітини від пошкоджень. Ці процеси можуть впливати й на стан шкіри, пояснює Гекман.
Кишковий мікробіом - спільнота мікроорганізмів, які живуть у нашому кишківнику, - також допомагає імунній системі працювати належним чином. А ще він може впливати на перебіг деяких шкірних захворювань.
Як підтримати його здоров'я? Насамперед харчуватися різноманітно.
Їжте більше овочів і фруктів, додавайте до меню бобові, цільнозернові продукти, зелень і спеції. Що різноманітніший ваш раціон, то більше поживних речовин отримує організм.
Таке харчування може позитивно впливати на сон і рівень стресу, а також допомагати підтримувати здоров'я шкіри.
Особливої уваги заслуговують ферментовані продукти. Це, наприклад, квашена капуста, кімчі, комбуча та йогурт.
Вони можуть підтримувати кишкову мікрофлору, а отже, допомагати зберігати нормальну роботу кишківника.
Тож не обов'язково шукати якісь екзотичні продукти. Іноді достатньо частіше їсти овочі, додати до сніданку йогурт або покласти на тарілку трохи квашеної капусти.
Як зберегти здоров'я шкіри з віком
Звісно, правильне харчування не зробить так, щоб у 60 років ми виглядали б на 30. Але воно може допомогти шкірі довше залишатися здоровою, пружною та добре зволоженою.
Що для цього робити?
- Щодня їсти різнокольорові овочі та фрукти.
- Додавати до раціону горіхи й насіння.
- Регулярно їсти жирну рибу.
- Не забувати про продукти, корисні для кишкової мікрофлори.
- Намагатися харчуватися різноманітно, а не зосереджуватися на одному "чудодійному" продукті.
І найголовніше - не забувайте про сонцезахисний крем. Навіть найкорисніший раціон не замінить захисту від ультрафіолету.
Турбота про шкіру починається не лише у ванній кімнаті перед дзеркалом. Вона починається і на нашій кухні - з простих щоденних звичок, які допомагають організму залишатися здоровим.
End of Підписуйтеся на нас у соцмережах
